newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Arabs gather to adopt anti-violence strategy.
newsitem.headline: Arabs gather to adopt anti-violence strategy.

text.p: Interior ministers from 20 Arab countries gathered in Tunis on Friday for a meeting over the weekend to approve a strategy to fight "terrorism", a term they generally use to refer to Moslem fundamentalist violence.

The approval of the final draft of the strategy will be one of the main issues on the agenda of the annual session of the Arab Interior Ministers Council on Saturday, the council's Secretary General Ahmed Mohamed Assalem told journalists .

The Tunis-based council is a specialised body of the Arab League. Since its establishment in 1980 it has been chaired by Saudi Arabia Interior Minister Prince Nayef bin Abdul-Aziz. He arrived in Tunis on Thursday.
Assalem said the final draft, which took more than two years of talks to agree, made member states "commit themselves to take effective and firm measures to ban and fight whatever form of terrorism".

These states also committed themselves that "their lands will not be used to plan, organise or carry out terrorist acts, and to strengthen controls to prevent the (crossborder) infiltration of terrorism and destructive elements or to smuggle ammunitions and explosives," he added.
The document also calls for close cooperation between member states in investigating and arresting suspects, as well as the freezing of all assets suspected of financing violent acts.
Assalem said the council's members had agreed on a definition of terrorist acts which clearly excluded armed struggle against foreign occupation.
"The draft reaffirms...Islam's call for leniency and moderation which repudiates all forms of crime and terrorism," he added.
